I recently dined at **The Glimmering Grotto**, a subterranean fantasy-themed restaurant tucked beneath the cobblestone streets of the old market quarter. From the moment you descend the candlelit spiral staircase, you’re enveloped in a world of faux-stalactites, softly glowing bioluminescent orbs, and the gentle sound of a trickling indoor waterfall. It’s undeniably theatrical, but somehow it never tips into tacky.

The menu is a playful fusion of foraged ingredients and molecular gastronomy, presented as “earth, sea, and sky.” I started with the **“Forest Floor”** — a stunning dish of truffle-infused mushroom pâté, edible moss (spinach powder and panko), and tiny meringue “pebbles” that dissolved on the tongue. It was earthy, rich, and surprisingly whimsical. For the main, I chose the **“Abyssal Feast”**: a perfectly seared piece of black cod on a bed of squid-ink risotto, surrounded by a foam that tasted of the sea and dotted with pearls of yuzu gel. The fish was buttery, the risotto al dente, and the citrus pearls cut through the richness beautifully.
